desc: Derive and prove the exact feasibility characterization for normalized directed intervals, including sufficiency and integer strictness.
Parse input and convert all `M` people into normalized intervals `[l, r]` with type `+`/`-`.
Implement iterative segment trees supporting point update, range maximum query, and range minimum query for active intervals by left and right endpoints.
Implement the sliding window with endpoint occupancy arrays, per-direction segment trees, `can_add`, `add`, `remove`, and compute `maxR[1..M]`.
Process the `Q` queries using `maxR`, output `Yes`/`No`, and test on samples plus edge cases such as shared endpoints, touching intervals, nested intervals, and opposite-direction crossings.
If sliding-window proof or implementation stalls, implement a nearest-conflict precomputation fallback using sweeps and RMQ/suffix minima.
